hook_text: Look at any pylon, crane or roof truss. They are full of triangles. Why not squares?
clip_script: Four paper struts make a square. Push the corner. It squashes flat! Three struts make a triangle. Push. Nothing moves. Add one strut across the square and it locks into two triangles. Now look around eMalahleni. Roof trusses: triangles. The crane on the building site: triangles. The bridge: triangles. That giant Eskom pylon: triangles, top to bottom. Engineers love triangles, because triangles do not wobble.
visual_style: Whiteboard square of struts squashing sideways into a diamond, then a diagonal strut snapping in to make two triangles; pylons, trusses, a crane and a bridge fade in, triangles highlighted.
pacing: The wobbly square, the locked triangle, then a quick tour of real structures full of triangles.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and count the triangles on the next pylon or roof you see.
